reverse_outline.summary: Three takeaways: catalog facts have separate owners and change rates; channel copies need a source and reconciliation; promises are computed once and frozen
One product page mixes facts that change at very different speeds, so a single update schedule leaves it wrong
One record per fact means four owners (content, price, discount, stock); search owns none and only shows copies
Where Eva's order stands: what catalog, search, price, stock and shipping must settle before add-to-cart
Each chapter opens on a Kestrel & Pine case where two copies of one fact disagreed
Roadmap of the five chapter questions in order
Product information chapter: PIM owns content and identifiers, separating products, variants, SKUs and barcodes
Pricing chapter: who selects prices; the €179 German error fixed by dated prices and source comparison
Promotions chapter: combining offers and carrying discounts to invoices/refunds (Black Friday stacking loss); separately, gift-card and loyalty balances kept apart
Search chapter: index as a maintained copy; better data and synonyms, not the engine, fix results
Inventory chapter: physical stock vs sellable availability; Black Friday oversell fixed by deriving availability from stock and commitments

reverse_outline.draft_locator: What the Five Answers Add Up To, and Where to Begin ¶1
reverse_outline.summary: Synthesis: every fact gets an owner and every copy a source; diagnose by asking which fact and owner; start with product information

results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
Every outline summary matches the controlling idea of the aligned spec paragraph (p01-p11); the KEY POINTS callout matches the evidence declared for p02.

results.quote: Gift-card and loyalty balances are kept apart.
results.finding: The outliner needed two phrases for this unit: the Black Friday stacking case, and 'separately' the gift-card and loyalty balances. The spec lists the balances in p08's idea, but the draft states them as a bare closing sentence with no link to the discounts the paragraph is about (P2-3: they are balances the merchant owes, not discounts), so they read as a second idea. Both flow readers also asked 'kept apart from what?'.
Each unit traces to the part thesis: p01-p02 state and illustrate the claim, p03-p05 place it and give the roadmap, p06-p10 introduce the chapters arguing P2-1 to P2-6, p11 synthesizes.

results.quote: A season entered four times motivates a **product information management system (PIM)**
results.finding: The case is given without what it shows (spec: with no owner for product content each system keeps its own version). The terms reader could not tell that 'entered four times' means typed into four systems, and both flow readers said this case did not read as two copies of one fact disagreeing, which p04 promises.

Figures 1 and 2 have captions that state what they show; the KEY POINTS callout, the €179/nine days/€8,200, 2,860 orders/€52,000, waterproof jacket and 1,340-jacket cases each come with what they show.

results.quote: Each chapter opens on a case at **Kestrel & Pine, the fictional outdoor brand** selling her jacket, where two copies of one fact disagreed.
results.finding: The declared relationship is contrast (Eva's order needs each fact right; the cases are where one was wrong). The sentence carries over 'her jacket' but signals no contrast; it reads as a further description, not as the turn from what must be right to where it went wrong.

results.quote: [[pricing-architecture]] decides **who selects a price and how channels receive it**.
results.finding: Declared: a sequence phrase at the start carrying over the variants the product chapter identified (prices are stored per variant). The paragraph opens with no phrase linking it to the product chapter; flow reader 2 noted that only the promotions and inventory paragraphs say why they come where they do. The decision log records the linking phrases as cut for length while the spec still declares them, so spec and draft disagree.

results.quote: [[commerce-search-and-discovery]] treats **the search index as a maintained copy** of product, price, stock and review data.
results.finding: Declared: contrast (content, price and discount each have an owner; the index holds copies of all of them). 'A maintained copy' implies the contrast but nothing marks the turn from owners to a holder of copies; both flow readers said it was unclear why search comes fourth. The decision log records the linking phrases as cut while the spec still declares this one.

The remaining boundaries express their declared relationships: p01->p02 elaboration ('Under Part I's rule of one record per fact'), p02->p03 place ('Where we are in the order's journey'), p04->p05 sequence ('The chapters ask, in order'), p05->chapters section elaboration, p07->p08 sequence ('starts from that price'), p09->p10 sequence ('comes last'), chapters->conclusion summary ('Together, the answers').

results.quote: **A promise is computed once, in one place, and then frozen.** The price is copied to the invoice, the discount allocated to every line of the order, and the last unit committed to exactly one order.
results.finding: Both flow readers found KEY POINTS bullet 3 floating: the body never returns to promises being computed once and frozen, and per-line allocation appears nowhere else. The spec declares that bullet 3 is carried by the KEY POINTS alone (p02a was cut), so the difficulty comes from the spec's content.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread item 2 (KEY POINTS bullet 3 'frozen ... allocated to every line'; body never returns to promises)

results.draft_locus: Introduction callout; Chapters in this part ¶5
results.quote: The €179 German price and the marketplace selling an empty shelf on Black Friday were copies nobody compared with their source.
results.finding: Both readers could not be sure the 'marketplace selling an empty shelf' is the same event as 'the Black Friday oversell of 1,340 jackets'; the body never mentions a marketplace, and flow reader 2 also notes the bullet names incidents before they are met.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread items 1 and 10 (KEY POINTS bullet 2 names incidents before met; marketplace vs oversell blur)

results.quote: Under Part I's rule of one record per fact, content, price, discount and stock need four owners, not one catalog: they change at different speeds.
results.finding: Both readers re-read this sentence to see how the rule and the different speeds combine into the claim; the colon carries the reasoning, and discount enters though the opening paragraph showed only description and stock.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread item 3 (same sentence: 'colon does a lot; re-read how two reasons combine')

results.quote: Search owns none and shows copies.
results.finding: Both readers found the sentence abrupt: search has not been mentioned before and enters in a fragment-like sentence; the search index is glossed only later, in Figure 2's caption.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread item 4 (same sentence: 'abrupt; new actor in fragment-like sentence')

results.quote: and her €235 basket must qualify for free shipping.
results.finding: Both readers could not tie free shipping to any chapter (it is meant as the discount fact, but the promotions paragraph never mentions it); reader 2 also stopped to reconcile €235 with €199.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread item 6 ('€235 vs €199 stopped to reconcile; free shipping not tied to a chapter')

results.quote: **Where we are in the order's journey.** Before Eva clicks "add to cart" on 13 April 2027
results.finding: Flow reader 1 felt the Eva paragraph, placed after Figure 2, breaks the move from the recommended shape to the roadmap and suggested moving it after the Kestrel & Pine sentence or after the opening. Flow reader 2 found its placement reasonable. The position is the spec's declared order.

results.quote: Each chapter opens on a case at **Kestrel & Pine, the fictional outdoor brand** selling her jacket, where two copies of one fact disagreed.
results.finding: Both readers found the promise not borne out: the season entered four times, the leftover campaign setting and the missing attributes and synonyms are not presented as two copies of one fact disagreeing. The spec intends each case as a copy disagreement (p06's evidence: each system keeps its own version), but the chapter paragraphs do not show it.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread item 7 (same sentence: 'not borne out')

results.quote: The chapters ask, in order: who owns product content and identifiers, who selects a price, how discounts combine and reach invoices and refunds, what feeds the search index, and what "in stock" means.
results.finding: Flow reader 1 found the roadmap stated twice in a row (the five questions, then the chapter list repeating them). Flow reader 2 did not report it. The spec keeps p05 deliberately for AC-1.

results.quote: Gift-card and loyalty balances are kept apart.
results.finding: Both readers asked 'kept apart from what?'.

results.quote: [[inventory-and-availability]] comes last and distinguishes **physical stock from what a channel may still sell**.
results.finding: Both readers marked the positions of search and inventory unclear: search copies stock, yet stock comes after it, and 'comes last' is stated without a reason. The spec's section rationale gives the reason (the part ends on the unit committed at checkout, where Part III begins), but the draft no longer says it.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, section notes ('unclear why search is fourth; inventory "comes last" stated but not explained') and lost-thread item 9

results.quote: dated prices and comparing copies with their source fix it.
results.finding: 'Dated prices' is never glossed, though does_not_know says effective-dated prices are glossed in a clause where the chapter list uses them. The terms reader and flow reader 1 (item 9, guessed 'effective dates') both did not understand it.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 1, lost-thread item 9 ('dated prices' not understood); also on does_not_know and never given

results.quote: **Every channel shows a copy, and a copy needs a source and a reconciliation.**
results.finding: 'Reconciliation' is used in KEY POINTS before anything explains it; the only gloss is in Figure 2's caption, and the body never introduces it (terms reader item 2).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread item 5 (Figure 2 caption: 'reconciliation' new concept; body never introduces it)

results.quote: the remedy derives availability from owned stock and commitments (units promised to orders).
results.finding: 'Owned stock' is ambiguous for the reader (owned by whom, or stock with an owner?) (terms reader item 14).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread item 11 ('unclear what "owned" stock means')

results.quote: the discount allocated to every line of the order
results.finding: 'Allocated to every line' (order lines, and why a discount is split across them) is not explained anywhere on the page (terms reader item 4).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread item 2 ('did not understand ... "allocated to every line"')

results.quote: **A promise is computed once, in one place, and then frozen.**
results.finding: 'Frozen' is never made concrete (terms reader item 5).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, lost-thread item 2 ('did not understand "frozen"')

results.quote: and the last unit committed to exactly one order.
results.finding: 'Committed' is used in KEY POINTS before 'commitments (units promised to orders)' is glossed in the inventory paragraph (terms reader item 5). The gloss is given later, and no flow reader reported the term.

results.quote: Missing attributes and synonyms hid a waterproof jacket
results.finding: The terms reader could only partly guess what 'attributes' and 'synonyms' mean for a search index (item 13). No flow reader reported it.
The introduction opens on a concrete product page (intriguing example), not a placeholder, restated question, dictionary definition, 'dawn of man' or book report.
The conclusion is short, opens on synthesis ('Together, the answers'), adds no new subtopic or evidence, and ends on a course of action, not a rephrased thesis.

It states what no single chapter paragraph states (each fact on the page gets an owner and each copy a source) and says why it matters ('When a page is wrong, ask first which fact is wrong and who owns it').
'each fact on the opening page' returns to the product page of p01; flow reader 2 said the callback lands.

From the introduction alone the reader named the five chapter subjects in order: product content and identifiers, price selection, how discounts combine and reach invoices and refunds, what feeds the search index, what 'in stock' means; it also predicted Kestrel & Pine cases, Eva's order and the figures as evidence, in a declarative tone. Matches the expected answer and the roadmap.

The reader answered that the description can stay the same for a season while the last unit can sell out with the page open, so one schedule leaves the page right about the product and wrong about buyability, which is why each fact has its own owner and update path. Matches the expected answer.

(a) commerce-promotions, for how offers combine and reach invoices and refunds (2,860 Black Friday orders); (b) commerce-search-and-discovery, the index as a maintained copy whose results depend on the attributes and synonyms fed in. Matches the expected answer.
